name: Octreotide
route_note: SC injection 2–3 times daily or IV infusion; monthly IM depot (LAR); oral delayed-release capsules for acromegaly

discovery.note: An eight-amino-acid cyclic peptide retaining the active core of somatostatin, with a half-life of hours rather than minutes.

tagline: A stable somatostatin mimic for acromegaly, carcinoid syndrome and variceal bleeding
summary: Octreotide is a synthetic eight-amino-acid analogue of somatostatin that inhibits secretion of growth hormone and many gut hormones. It treats acromegaly and the symptoms of neuroendocrine tumours, slows their growth, and is widely used to control bleeding from oesophageal varices.
mechanism: Octreotide binds somatostatin receptors, mainly SSTR2 and SSTR5, which are Gi-coupled receptors that lower cAMP and calcium influx and inhibit hormone exocytosis. In the pituitary it reduces growth hormone and therefore IGF-1; in the gut and pancreas it suppresses serotonin, gastrin, VIP, insulin and glucagon.

It also reduces splanchnic blood flow and portal pressure, and has antiproliferative effects on neuroendocrine tumour cells. Oral Mycapssa uses a transient permeability enhancer to allow intestinal absorption.
uses: Symptoms of carcinoid tumours (flushing, diarrhoea) and VIPomas
Acute oesophageal variceal bleeding (off-label in US, standard practice)
Prevention of complications after pancreatic surgery (some countries)

history.title: Somatostatin discovered
history.detail: Roger Guillemin's group isolates somatostatin, whose very short half-life limits therapeutic use.

history.title: Octreotide synthesised
history.detail: Bauer and colleagues at Sandoz report SMS 201-995.

history.title: Monthly depot
history.detail: Sandostatin LAR depot is approved in the US.

history.title: PROMID
history.detail: The PROMID trial shows octreotide LAR prolongs time to progression in midgut neuroendocrine tumours.

history.title: Oral octreotide
history.detail: FDA approves Mycapssa, the first oral somatostatin analogue, for acromegaly in June 2020.

pk.bioavailability: 100% SC; under 1% oral (enhanced with Mycapssa formulation)

facts: Native somatostatin has a half-life of 1–3 minutes, compared with nearly 2 hours for octreotide.
Radiolabelled octreotide analogues are used for imaging and for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy of neuroendocrine tumours.
